summary: Cybernews researchers found that Hong Kong developer Imagime Interactive Limited left a Kafka Broker instance used by its AI companion apps Chattee Chat and GiMe Chat exposed to the internet without authentication or access controls. It held more than 43 million intimate messages and over 600,000 images and videos from over 400,000 users, plus user logs, in-app purchase records, IP addresses, device identifiers and authentication tokens; no names or email addresses. The server was secured after Cybernews disclosed it; the findings were published in October 2025.
